title: Can LLMs predict the outcomes of machine learning experiments?
abstract: arXiv:2610.22599v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent advances in AI make Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) increasingly plausible. Large Language Models (LLMs) can already propose, select, and run Machine Learning (ML) experiments. However, the space of possible design choices in ML is vast. An LLM that proposes an experiment needs a reliable intuition of whether it is worth running given the timing constraints of long training runs. In this work, we measure such intuition in current frontier LLMs by evaluating how accurately they predict the impact of self-generated ML experiment ideas before these are put into training runs. To this end, we construct a dataset of 288 LLM-proposed ideas on eight MLE-bench tasks. We then prompt five frontier LLMs (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.3) to predict the impact of each idea and compare their predictions with the actual outcomes after training. translated_title: 大语言模型能预测机器学习实验的结果吗？
translated_abstract: 人工智能的最新进展使得递归自我改进（RSI）越来越具有可行性。大语言模型（LLM）已经能够提出、选择并运行机器学习（ML）实验。然而，机器学习中可能的设计选择空间非常庞大。提出实验的LLM需要具备可靠的直觉，以便在长训练时间的限制下判断某个实验是否值得运行。在这项工作中，我们通过评估当前前沿LLM在实验投入训练之前预测其自生成的机器学习实验想法影响力的准确程度，来衡量这种直觉。为此，我们构建了一个包含288个LLM提出的实验想法的数据集，涵盖八个MLE-bench任务。随后，我们提示五个前沿LLM（GPT-6 Astra、Claude Opus 5.5、Claude Fable 5.1、Kimi K3和GLM-5.3）预测每个想法的影响力，并将其预测与训练后的实际结果进行比较。我们报告了四个主要发现。首先，LLM的预测相当……
tldr: 该论文构建了包含288个LLM自生成实验想法的数据集，通过让五个前沿大语言模型在机器学习实验训练前预测其影响力并与实际结果对比，衡量了这些模型判断实验是否值得运行的直觉准确性。
en_tdlr: This paper measures the intuition of five frontier LLMs by evaluating how accurately they predict the impact of 288 self-generated ML experiment ideas across eight MLE-bench tasks before training, comparing their predictions with actual outcomes.
